shared.problem: The active renderer accepts sufficiently long unrelated text and unlocks feedback and stage credit. Explore also hides sentence notes until this gate is passed.
shared.correction: Check focused decisions objectively where possible. Label authentic open responses as attempts or self-review. Keep sentence notes available as learning support.
shared.savedProgressAffected: Preserve notes and drafts. Do not count a legacy length-gate completion as a new checked answer.

shared.problem: The score distinguishes correct decisions, but a finished run counts towards stage completion at any score and unlocks Master writing. A checked wrong answer receives an explanation with no item-level retry.
shared.correction: Show first-try, retry and supported outcomes explicitly. Keep diagnostic feedback and practice accessible at any score.
shared.savedProgressAffected: Use new assessment identities or versions when scoring changes and retain unaffected progress.

pedagogy-q-019.problem: Neither event has an end time and the bus stop travel time is missing. Even the demonstration could run past 5:30.
pedagogy-q-019.correction: Give both finish times and the walking time. Ask which advice fits students who need to finish an activity and reach the stop by 5:30.
pedagogy-q-019.savedProgressAffected: Version the revised item. Preserve writing drafts and earlier course progress.

pedagogy-q-007.problem: The stem gives away the sorting labels. The answers use compressed fragments and the single decision duplicates Silver-level grouping.
pedagogy-q-007.correction: Provide a school magazine brief for a group visit, competing evidence about accessibility and costs, and readable two-paragraph plans with plausible reasons for each.
pedagogy-q-007.savedProgressAffected: Version the revised item and preserve the separate Master draft.

pedagogy-q-006.problem: Students see the racket paragraph but have to assume there is a paragraph about the courts.
pedagogy-q-006.correction: Show the existing paragraph headings and ask which detail to move and where.

pedagogy-extra-q-8.problem: The key assumes a value paragraph that the source never introduces.
pedagogy-extra-q-8.correction: Show both the teaching paragraph and a planned costs paragraph. Ask where the entrance fee belongs.

cohesion-q-010.problem: The learner has to interpret ‘keeps the restriction’ before attempting the grammar decision.
cohesion-q-010.correction: Ask which version makes clear that only courses with coaching cost extra. Review the options for competing valid formulations.

editing-q-003.problem: ‘Most useful diagnosis’ adds terminology to a straightforward repetition question.
editing-q-003.correction: Ask what the writer should fix in the two sentences. Give feedback that explains why the exact waiting time is worth keeping once.

exam-q-002.problem: ‘Reader need should drive the judgement’ makes the instructions harder than choosing the audience-specific answer.
exam-q-002.correction: Ask what younger viewers will want to know. Keep the school-magazine brief visible and compare equally plausible film-review priorities.

cohesion-task-002.problem: The model has 36 whitespace-delimited words against the stated target of about 40–60.
cohesion-task-002.correction: Align the model and target without adding unsupplied details. Make the change from game features to yesterday’s experience visible.

pedagogy-extra-q-31.problem: Both the keyed advice to try it if you enjoy realistic characters and the advice to avoid it if you prefer fast-paced films balance the same evidence. The stem gives student readers no preference that would distinguish the two.
pedagogy-extra-q-31.correction: Name a reader priority or accept both justified recommendations using an interaction built for multiple valid decisions.

pedagogy-extra-q-27.problem: Five-minute service during a twenty-minute break does not establish whether students can reach the café, eat and return to class. The key asserts that they can.
pedagogy-extra-q-27.correction: Include walking time and an explicit reader decision, or say that the quick service leaves fifteen minutes for travel and eating.

pedagogy-extra-q-30.problem: The preferred answer implies sharing may cut practice time, but sharing a bench does not establish that beginners take turns to use tools or have less time. The other balanced option also addresses both facts.
pedagogy-extra-q-30.correction: Specify that only one person can use the bench at a time, then name a beginner priority and distinguish the options by their use of that evidence.

pedagogy-extra-q-13.problem: Both distractors are implausible word combinations that would rarely occur in an actual learner review.
pedagogy-extra-q-13.correction: Use natural phrases that describe different effects of a film and ask which one matches the stated effect on the viewer.

pedagogy-extra-q-18.problem: The third option also avoids attacking staff. Its formality is the only signal that it falls short, and the register language makes the comparison very easy.
pedagogy-extra-q-18.correction: Give a brief excerpt with useful evidence and compare natural alternatives that differ in whether they turn it into fair, useful advice.
